body.heading: Specific beats general
paragraphs: 'You're great' is pleasant and forgettable. 'Thank you for handling the school email — I know those make you anxious and you did it anyway' is neither. Specific appreciation tells the other person you actually see their life, which is most of what appreciation is for.
The formula is simple: name the thing, name what it cost or meant. It takes one sentence and about five seconds of thought.

body.heading: Say it when it is small
paragraphs: Most kindness in a shared life is small and logistical: the bin taken out, the form filled in, the cup of tea that arrived unasked. Waiting for grand occasions to say thank you means the daily fabric of care goes unmentioned — and unmentioned care slowly becomes invisible care.
Out loud matters. A thought is a nice intention; a sentence is an event. Say it at the time, in passing, without making a ceremony of it.

body.heading: Receiving is a skill too
paragraphs: When appreciation comes your way, let it land: 'thank you' is a complete answer. Deflecting it — 'it was nothing' — quietly taxes the giver. Receiving warmly encourages the whole exchange to happen again, in both directions.

description: Specific, prompt, spoken appreciation makes the everyday care in a relationship visible instead of assumed.
